title: Reconstruction-independent moment tests for sample-based spectral functions — reproduction repository
description:
Reproduction deposit for N. Bonilla Vargas, Reconstruction-independent moment tests for sample-based spectral functions, manuscript prepared for SciPost Physics Core (deposit 2.0.0, 2026-10-02). It contains the manuscript sources, the exact sector-Lanczos/Haydock engine and every generator behind the quoted numbers and figures, the deposited data (one dated JSON per computation), the hash-sealed pre-registrations and records of the blinded calibration and of the on-device nk test (which submitted no device job), the raw counts and submitted circuits of the IBM Quantum (ibm_fez) jobs, a smoke test with a record check (python src/verify.py), Makefile targets and a notebook that run the generators. Every moment in the work is evaluated classically; the device supplies only sampled supports. What does not regenerate exactly from source is listed in docs/REPRODUCE.md (Known gaps). Code under the MIT licence; manuscript, data and documentation under CC BY 4.0; the SciPost template files keep their own terms.

Summary of the work. How can a spectral function A(ω) from sample-based quantum diagonalization be tested without trusting it? Not with its own moments, which agree with it by construction, but with full-operator moments ⟨J†(H−e0)kJ⟩ of the probe J on the subspace ground state, of energy e0. We prove that the two differ exactly by the probe state's leak out of the subspace: the missed weight at k=0, and zero through order 2K+1 when the subspace holds the probe state's order-K Krylov space. Off an eigenstate the operator form matters: a lone commutator-form m1 check can pass a first moment 11% low. The m1 and m2 checks detect weight moved in frequency at fixed total weight, which captured weight cannot see. Scored against a numerical tolerance, this deterministic leak flags almost every sampled support and does not track the error, so detection and false-positive rates use exact moments plus shot noise. In a pre-registered blinded simulation, the m0–m2 test rejected all 56 truncations, 20 of 34 weight-preserving spurious features and none of 71 under-converged Krylov spectra. Its false-positive rate was 1/112, or 40/112 under the pre-registered 1.96-fold larger noise. No m0–m2 check is guaranteed to detect weight moved among four or more fixed poles, and full-support Rayleigh–Ritz passes the default thresholds with relative L1 error 0.93. On IBM Heron samples, with all moments computed classically, captured weight rewards support spreading, not fidelity.
